statement: A transformation changes only the aura: both fighters play the same three placeholder poses for every form and no body look is keyed to a form.
depends_on: F-COMBAT-08 (which forms exist in the sim)
risk: A body change per form can break the look gate or the flash checks; a still per tier per fighter shows it early.
orb_question: Is an aura change enough for a transformation in Alpha, or must the body change too? Recommendation: one cheap body change per step carried by data (hair or accent colour and each fighter's own break pose), bulked-up bodies after Alpha.

statement: In a 2v2 the two copies of each fighter are drawn identically, and the mirror match is held off for the same missing second colour.
risk: A fix that writes a new colour into the fighter's sim fields would change the hash; keep it in the renderer's lane-colour remap (render/core/look.gd:930-939).
orb_question: In a 2v2, how should the second copy of a fighter differ? Recommendation: a second body colour per fighter from Art, picked by team, not a marker over the fighter.

statement: The animation check that holds the joint gate is in no CI job and has no saved record on the tree that was landed as 6a30b4c9.
risk: The check is 8,300 lines and its run time in CI is not known; time it once before adding it.

statement: The animation coverage table is of 2026-10-03, was built from Combat's then-parked files, still marks 180 of 228 rows parked, and its check runs in no gate.
risk: A regenerated table can pass on data while a cell still plays a walked pick in a match; the live probe is the proof.

statement: The creative rulebook's held-pose rows still fail the animation check, which is a line of the EP's full gate, against the project rule that they never block a gate.
risk: Splitting the held-pose test out of the check could drop the joint gate by accident; the check's negative control shows it.
orb_question: Should a failed held-pose rule stop a change from landing? Recommendation: no, report it as a warning and keep only the joint limits as a hard stop.

statement: The rulebook's three questions to Orb (which numbers move, a named-exception list, who signs a change) are unanswered, so every threshold is still Legal's first guess.
The animation runtime, its tools and its data (render/anim, data/anim) are on no director's owns line; Animation owns only art/animation and docs/animation.
The rival's four tail strikes sit in his live pools as waiting rows with no key set and no tail bones in the rig.
risk: Only one skip of waiting rows was read (blur.gd:213); another pool reader without the skip would pick a blow with no animation.

statement: Animation's parked-work page still says Parked for patches the inventory found on main, and the wave files' own headers still say no live match plays them.
Every strike piece Combat's data names resolves to that fighter's own key set (79 of 79 and 80 of 84), and the 39 names both fighters use resolve to different key sets.
Joint limits are data, are enforced by a last pass on every solve with the limit on by default, and passed the animation check one tree before the baseline.
The creative rulebook exists as a page with its 83 rows, owned by Animation with Art, and Legal's handover is on file.
The two different fighters read apart by body, hair and aura colour, by idle and by timing, which Orb accepted for the first Alpha.
